module: luaqrcode (Patrick Gundlach / speedata, BSD 3-clause license): pure-Lua QR code generator. It picks the smallest version (1 to 40) and the mode (numeric, alphanumeric, binary), encodes the data, computes the Reed-Solomon error correction, generates the 8 masks and keeps the one with the lowest penalty. It draws nothing: it returns a matrix of modules that the modder displays themselves (for example in UI or a texture).
usage:
local qr = require('libs/luaqrcode/qrencode')
local ok, matrix = qr.qrcode('https://beamng.com')
if ok then
  for x = 1, #matrix do for y = 1, #matrix do
    local noir = matrix[x][y] > 0
  end end
end
notes: Matrix values: positive = black module, negative = white module (1/-1 for data, 2/-2 for mandatory patterns). The matrix is indexed matrix[x][y], 1-based, square of size 4 * version + 17; [1][1] is top left.

qrcode returns (true, matrix) on success, (false, message) if the arranged data is not a multiple of 8 bits; other failure cases (text too long for version 40, etc.) may raise an error (inferred from code).

The mode parameter is not implemented: passing it triggers assert(false, 'not implemented') in get_version_eclevel_mode_bistringlength. The mode is chosen automatically: numeric if only digits, alphanumeric for [0-9A-Z $%*./:+-], otherwise binary.
ec_level error correction levels: 1 to 4 (L, M, Q, H). Without a value, the function takes the highest level that fits in the smallest version.
The file contains an 'if testing' block that exports internal functions if the global testing is defined; otherwise only qrcode is exported.

qrcode.desc: Generates the QR code of a string: determines version, error correction level and mode, encodes the data, adds the error correction, then picks the lowest-penalty mask.

ec_level.desc: Requested error correction level, 1 to 4 (L, M, Q, H). Optional.

mode.desc: Not implemented: do not provide it (causes an assertion).

returns.desc: Matrix [x][y] of modules (positive = black), or error message if the first return value is false.
